blindSummary:
Practical risk here is modest: far safer than the neighbouring state, with no criminalisation of trans identity, no religious police, and one of the world's lowest crime rates. The penal provision that criminalised sex between men was repealed in 2022, and the prison service reports no assaults against its 10 transgender inmates — unusually positive for axis-H. The country is also a regional medical hub with gender-affirming care available.

The main gaps: legal gender recognition requires genital surgery (expensive and restrictive), there is no general anti-discrimination law — a 2025 workplace-fairness law explicitly excludes sexual orientation and gender identity — and over 65% of trans residents report negative workplace experiences. A broadcast code still groups homosexuality with "paedophilia and incest" as lifestyles barred from the airwaves. Progress has "stalled" since the 2022 repeal, with discrimination "quietly tolerated."

For a visitor: efficient border processing, very low street crime, unrestricted bathrooms, and no trans-specific police friction. The atmosphere is conservative but quietly accommodating in practice.
blindOutOfScope: General crime is extremely low; no trans-specific travel advisory.
blindSourceSummaries: National trans organisation, a support network and a national university's study of public sentiments toward and challenges faced by the transgender and gender-diverse community (Feb 2025): comprehensive survey covering demographics, school experiences, employment barriers and discrimination, healthcare access, gender-affirming care costs and experiences, and cisgender perspectives.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the criminalisation of sex between men was repealed in 2022 (effective January 2023), but the constitution was simultaneously amended to codify marriage as between a man and a woman; adoption restrictions; trans people can change gender markers conditional on gender-affirming surgery; trans youth can access HRT with both parents' consent (16+ private, 18+ public), with much stricter access under 21.

National daily (Nov 2023): 10 transgender inmates behind bars (one post-surgery, nine transitioning), with no assaults reported, per the national prison service - raised in parliament after a case in another country involving a transgender woman in women's accommodation; housing arrangements discussed.

Pride-organisation statement (Jan 2025): the new workplace-fairness legislation conspicuously and explicitly excludes sexual orientation and gender identity - 'leaves the LGBTQ+ community empty-handed yet again'; a 2024 study by the same movement found 69% of LGBTQ+ people encountered discrimination or harassment in hiring or at work; trans workers face some of the most severe discrimination including hiring barriers and safety threats.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying news-agency feature (June 2023) covers the LGBT community here feeling safer as the end of the criminalisation of sex between men brings change.

Foreign regional daily (July 2025): this country's radio broadcast code groups homosexuality with paedophilia and incest as 'lifestyles' not allowed on air - a former DJ and a blogger call for review, saying the clause 'has no place' after the repeal.
Country profile from an international LGBT-rights barometer project: composite LGBT-rights perception scores including a transgender-rights index.

A travel company's country guide: LGBTQIA+ travellers here are largely welcomed and supported, though discretion with public displays of affection is recommended; annual support rallies since 2009 and a friendly bar scene are noted.

Community-news report (Jan 2006): the government awarded a grant of 100,000 units of the local currency to a group claiming to help gays and lesbians 'understand' their sexual identity - the community outlet uncovered its links to an international religiously-affiliated ex-gay/reparative-therapy network; its founder is a self-described ex-transsexual.
blindLocalsOnly: The surgery-required legal-gender-recognition regime, the workplace-fairness law exclusion, and the 65% negative-workplace-experience figure are resident-facing; the prison-service data concerns resident inmates.
blindTangential: The broadcast code grouping homosexuality with "paedophilia and incest" is a climate signal; the 2022 repeal of the sodomy provision removed partner-related criminal exposure for visitors.
